status_note: substrait-io/substrait-validator#608 (open) asks to implement the precision temporal types; the validator reports their literals as not implemented, at error level.
title: substrait-validator rejects precision_time and precision_timestamp literals as unimplemented
summary: `substrait-validator` reports a `precision_time` or `precision_timestamp` literal with an error, `not yet implemented: PrecisionTimestamp literals are not yet implemented` (code 0001), so a plan with a time or timestamp constant is never valid to it. The types themselves get a warning only. Substrait has used the precision temporal types since the plain `time` and `timestamp` were deprecated, so every plan with a timestamp constant meets it.
repro: Export a plan that compares a timestamp column with a constant (the coverage case `time/compare with literal`: `t.filter(t.ts > ibis.timestamp("2024-01-01 00:00:00"))`) and validate it: `python -m sverify_dev.substrait_validator --only "compare with literal"`.
handling: Recorded in `python/tests/substrait_validator.json`: the plans with such literals are `disagree` with this record, and the gate (`sverify_dev.substrait_validator --check`) passes on them.
found_by: sverify_dev.substrait_validator, the validation of every plan to_substrait exports (#862)

checked.note: rs/src/parse/expressions/literals.rs still reports both literals as not implemented; #608 open
